subjects: Public authorities within the Ombudsperson Act
steps: Ombudsperson investigation where jurisdiction and discretionary criteria are met
routes.serves: People affected by administrative acts of covered authorities
routes.limitations: Specific statutory exclusions, appeal availability and timing apply.

steps: Request records from the statutory head
Ask Information and Privacy Commissioner for review
Inquiry and binding order where authorized; judicial review remains separate
routes.serves: People seeking access to records or protection of personal information
routes.limitations: Class coverage, record exclusions, exemptions and time limits differ; an FOI head is not a general parent.

steps: Review Division for reviewable Board decisions
Judicial review of qualifying final decisions
routes.locator: Workers Compensation Act ss.270,288–289,296; applicable review/judicial-review provisions
routes.serves: Workers, employers and other parties affected by compensation and occupational-safety decisions
routes.limitations: Not every decision follows the same route; statutory exceptions and direct appeals exist.

steps: Fair Practices Commissioner or Ombudsperson after other fairness avenues
routes.locator: WorkSafeBC Issue Resolution Office page; Fair Practices Commissioner page
routes.serves: Workers, employers and service users concerned about fairness
routes.limitations: These address fairness; they do not replace the Review Division/WCAT merits route.

steps: Health authority Patient Care Quality Office
Patient Care Quality Review Board review
Recommendations to health authority and/or minister
routes.locator: Patient Care Quality Review Board Act ss.2–4,13–15; External Complaint Regulation
routes.serves: Patients and people raising health-care-quality concerns
routes.limitations: External complaints excluded by regulation and other statutory routes must be separated; no general power to award compensation.

routes.serves: Employees, employers and parties to employment-standards determinations
routes.limitations: Appeal grounds are statutory; this is not a fresh hearing of every employment dispute.

steps: Statutory review consideration where qualifying grounds exist
routes.locator: Residential Tenancy Act ss.78.1–82; Judicial Review Procedure Act s.2
routes.serves: Tenants and landlords within the Act
routes.limitations: Review and judicial review are distinct; jurisdiction and statutory exclusions must be checked.

steps: Appeal to Property Assessment Appeal Board
Stated case to Supreme Court on a question of law
routes.serves: Owners and other statutorily entitled parties affected by assessed values
routes.limitations: The specific statutory standing, grounds and deadlines apply.

routes.locator: Labour Relations Code s.141; Judicial Review Procedure Act
routes.serves: Unions, employers, workers and other affected parties
routes.limitations: Reconsideration is not automatic: new evidence or inconsistency with labour-law principles, and statutory timing, matter.

steps: Appeal to tribunal for appealable reconsidered decisions
routes.locator: Employment and Assistance Act ss.17–21, including s.19.3
routes.serves: Applicants and recipients of income assistance; applicable disability-assistance cases
routes.limitations: Program eligibility and which decisions are appealable must be checked against the relevant Act.

steps: Judicial review of decision where available
routes.locator: Human Rights Code ss.21,27,31; Commissioner provisions in Part 3
routes.serves: People alleging discrimination in areas protected by the Code, and responding parties
routes.limitations: The Commissioner has separate public-interest functions and is not an appeal tribunal over Tribunal decisions.

steps: Fair Practices Office for unresolved service concerns
Civil Resolution Tribunal for eligible Enhanced Accident Benefits disputes
routes.locator: ICBC disputes about injury benefits page
routes.serves: Injured people seeking covered accident benefits
routes.limitations: ICBC’s published route distinguishes service/fairness concerns from statutory entitlement disputes; not every ICBC issue is a CRT matter.

routes.serves: People dealing with BC Housing programs and services
routes.limitations: A housing provider that receives BC Housing funding is not thereby the same legal respondent as BC Housing.

steps: Unresolved process-related complaint to BC Ferries Commissioner as described in approved process
routes.locator: Customer complaints process; Coastal Ferry Act s.45.2
routes.limitations: The Commissioner’s regulatory role and scope differ from an Ombudsperson investigation; Coastal Ferry Act s.75 excludes the ordinary Ombudsperson route.

steps: Police Complaint Commissioner oversight; statutory review/hearing mechanisms
routes.locator: Police Act Part 11, including ss.77 and following; s.72
routes.serves: People affected by conduct of police members within Part 11 jurisdiction
routes.limitations: RCMP complaints use a different federal framework; do not merge these routes.

steps: Use applicable statutory reconsideration or appeal
Apply to Supreme Court for judicial review when available
routes.locator: Judicial Review Procedure Act s.2; Administrative Tribunals Act application depends on enabling statute
routes.serves: People with standing to challenge the legality of an administrative decision
routes.limitations: This is a general legal route, not an assertion that every private corporate act or every public-service complaint is reviewable.

scope: Verified route families; not a complete body-by-body or historical legal-opinion table. No filing deadlines are supplied as individualized advice.
remaining: Enablement and incorporation of Administrative Tribunals Act provisions, appeal exclusions and historical versions require per-tribunal review for bodies not expressly listed.
